learn.hook: Can you count 23 cricket fans without losing track? Tally marks make it easy!
points: A tally mark is one small line for each thing you count.
After 4 standing lines, the 5th line goes across them. That makes a bundle of 5.
To read a tally, count the bundles in 5s: 5, 10, 15 ... then add the single lines.
Tallies help us count things that keep coming, like cars passing by.

example.q: Riya's tally for red cars has 2 bundles of five and 3 single lines. How many red cars did she see?
steps: Now count on the single lines: 11, 12, 13.

learn.reallife: Teachers use tallies to count votes for the class monitor, and scorers use them to count runs in a gully cricket match.

games.title: Match the tally to the number

quiz.q: Arjun's tally has 2 bundles of five and 4 single lines. What number does it show?
quiz.explain: Two bundles of five make 10. Four more lines make 14.
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1 instead of 5

quiz.q: How many lines are there in one full tally bundle?
quiz.explain: A bundle has 4 standing lines and 1 line across them. That is 5 lines.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count the line that goes across

quiz.q: Meena counted 17 kites. Which tally shows 17?
quiz.explain: 3 bundles of five make 15, and 2 more lines make 17.
steps: Answer: 3 bundles of five and 2 lines
quiz.mistake: Thinks each line or bundle stands for the digits of the number

quiz.q: In a class vote, mango got 4 full tally bundles and nothing else. How many votes did mango get?
quiz.explain: Each bundle is 5 votes. Counting in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20.
quiz.mistake: Counts the bundles but not the lines inside them

quiz.q: Aisha has 9 stickers. How many FULL bundles of five will her tally have?
quiz.explain: 9 is 5 and 4 more. So there is 1 full bundle and 4 single lines.
steps: One bundle of 5, then 4 single lines
quiz.mistake: Rounds 9 up to 10 and thinks there are 2 bundles

quiz.q: Why do we draw the 5th tally line across the other four?
options: It means we must stop counting
It makes groups of 5 so we can count quickly
quiz.explain: Crossing the 5th line makes a neat bundle of 5, so we can count in 5s instead of one by one.
steps: We cross the 5th line over 4 standing lines.
Then we can count bundles in 5s: 5, 10, 15 ...
It does not cancel or stop the count.
Answer: It makes groups of 5 so we can count quickly
quiz.mistake: Thinks a crossed line means rubbing out

quiz.q: Harpreet's tally of birds has 3 bundles of five and 1 line. Joseph's has 3 bundles of five and 4 lines. How many more birds did Joseph count?
quiz.explain: Harpreet counted 16 and Joseph counted 19. 19 − 16 = 3 more.
quiz.mistake: Gives Joseph's total instead of the difference

quiz.q: A scorer's tally of runs shows 6 full bundles of five. How many runs is that?
quiz.explain: Count in 5s six times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 and 5 instead of counting six fives

teach.ask: Gappu is counting mangoes with lines and his page is a mess! How do tally marks work?
teach.praise: Wow! Now I can count all the mangoes in fives. Chirp chirp!
teach.nudge: But what do I do when I reach the fifth line?

revise.summary: A tally mark is one line for each thing we count. The 5th line goes across 4 lines to make a bundle of 5. Count bundles in 5s, then add the single lines.
focus: Draw tally marks with the 5th line across.
Read a tally: count bundles in 5s, then count on the single lines.
Use tallies to count things that keep coming, like cars.
remember: One tally line = one thing.
One bundle = 5 lines.
2 bundles and 3 lines = 5, 10, then 11, 12, 13 = 13.
traps: Don't count a bundle as 1. It is 5.
Don't forget the line that goes across. It is the 5th line.
A crossed line is not rubbing out.

learn.hook: Long ago, shepherds had no numbers. So how did they know if every cow came home?
points: Make one mark for every cow that goes out. One cow, one mark.
When a cow comes back, strike off one mark.
Marks left that are not struck off show cows still missing.
We can do the same for children going out of the class and coming back.
For a big herd, like 36 cows and 23 sheep, make a separate set of marks for each animal.

example.q: Deba made 12 marks in the morning. In the evening he struck off 9 marks. How many cows are still out?
steps: Each struck-off mark is a cow that came back.

learn.reallife: A watchman at a school gate can make a mark for each child who leaves and strike it off when the child returns.

games.title: Mark or strike?
items: We make a new mark when a cow goes out.
One mark for each cow that leaves.
We make a new mark when a cow comes back.
When a cow comes back we strike off a mark.
If no marks are left un-struck, all cows are back.
Every mark was matched with a returning cow.
5 marks left means 5 cows came back.
Marks left over show cows that are still missing.

quiz.q: Deep's cows go out to graze. What should he do for each cow that goes out?
quiz.explain: Each cow going out gets one new mark. This matches one mark to one cow.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up going out with coming back

quiz.q: 14 cows went out, so Deba made 14 marks. In the evening 14 marks were struck off. How many cows are missing?
quiz.explain: Every mark was struck off, so every cow came back. None are missing.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the struck-off marks are missing cows

quiz.q: 11 marks were made for cows going out. 8 marks are struck off. How many cows are still out?
quiz.explain: Struck-off marks are cows that came back. The 3 marks left are cows still out.
steps: Marks made for cows going out = 11
Struck-off marks = cows that came back = 8
quiz.mistake: Gives the number that came back

quiz.q: Ms Rao makes a mark each time a child goes out of class. She strikes one off when the child comes back. She has 6 marks and 4 are struck off. How many children are outside?
quiz.explain: 4 children came back. 6 − 4 = 2 are still outside.
steps: Marks made = children who went out = 6
Struck-off marks = children who came back = 4
quiz.mistake: Adds the marks instead of taking away

quiz.q: A herd has 36 cows and 23 sheep. How many marks are needed for all the animals?
quiz.explain: One mark for each animal: 36 + 23 = 59 marks.
quiz.mistake: Takes away instead of adding

quiz.q: For the herd of 36 cows and 23 sheep, why is it smart to keep cow marks and sheep marks separate?
options: Because sheep do not need marks
So we can see which kind of animal is missing
quiz.explain: Separate sets show if a cow or a sheep is missing, not just that some animal is missing.
steps: Answer: So we can see which kind of animal is missing
quiz.mistake: Thinks the marks only tell the total

quiz.q: 23 sheep went out. In the evening 19 sheep marks were struck off. How many sheep are still out?
quiz.explain: 23 − 19 = 4 marks are not struck off, so 4 sheep are still out.
steps: Marks struck off = sheep that came back = 19
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers

quiz.q: Deba has 9 marks. He strikes off one mark for each cow that returns. 9 cows return and then 1 more cow walks in! What does this tell him?
options: A cow that was not his has come in
quiz.explain: There are only 9 marks, so only 9 of his cows went out. A 10th cow has no mark to match. It must be someone else's cow!
steps: Answer: A cow that was not his has come in
quiz.mistake: Thinks extra animals can always be matched

teach.ask: Gappu's 10 chicks went out to play. How can he check if they all came back without counting?
teach.praise: Clever! One mark for each chick, strike one off when it comes home. Chirp!
teach.nudge: But what do the marks that are left over tell me?

revise.summary: Make one mark for each cow that goes out. Strike off one mark when a cow comes back. Marks left show how many are still out.
focus: Match one mark to one animal or child.
Find how many are still out: marks made − marks struck off.
Use a separate set of marks for each kind of animal.
remember: One cow, one mark.
Still out = marks made − marks struck off.
12 marks, 9 struck off: 12 − 9 = 3 still out.
traps: Struck-off marks are the ones that came back, not the missing ones.
Don't add the numbers. Take away.

learn.hook: Your name is full of maths! How many letters does yours have?
points: We can count the letters in a name one by one.
Some names are short, like RIYA (4 letters). Some are long, like HARPREET (8 letters).
A table helps us write down counts neatly.
We can use tally marks to count how many children have names of each length.

example.q: How many letters are in the name JOSEPH?
steps: Point and count: J-1, O-2, S-3, E-4, P-5, H-6.

learn.reallife: When you fill your name in a form, there are boxes for each letter. Counting letters tells you how many boxes you need!

games.title: Name facts
items: RIYA has more letters than KABIR.
RIYA has 4 letters and KABIR has 5.
The letter A comes 2 times in AISHA.
A-I-S-H-A has A at the start and at the end.
MEENA and AISHA have the same number of letters.

quiz.q: How many letters are in the name KABIR?
quiz.explain: K-A-B-I-R. Counting them gives 5 letters.
steps: Point and count each letter of KABIR.
quiz.mistake: Skips or double-counts a letter

quiz.q: How many letters are in HARPREET?
quiz.explain: H-A-R-P-R-E-E-T has 8 letters. R and E both come twice, so count each one.
steps: Point and count each letter. Count repeated letters each time.
quiz.mistake: Counts a repeated letter only once

quiz.q: Which name has the MOST letters?
quiz.explain: JOSEPH has 6 letters. ARJUN has 5, and RIYA and NEHA have 4 each.
steps: Count the letters in each name.
quiz.mistake: Picks a name without counting all the letters

quiz.q: How many times does the letter A come in the name AISHA?
quiz.explain: A-I-S-H-A: there is an A at the start and another at the end. That is 2.
steps: Look at each letter: A yes, I no, S no, H no, A yes
quiz.mistake: Only notices the first A

quiz.q: Children in a group: Aisha, Arjun, Riya, Ankit, Meena. How many names start with A?
quiz.explain: Aisha, Arjun and Ankit start with A. Riya and Meena do not. That makes 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts names that have an A anywhere, not just at the start

quiz.q: MEENA has 5 letters. RIYA has 4 letters. How many letters do they have together?
quiz.explain: Put the two counts together: 5 + 4 = 9 letters.
steps: MEENA has 5 letters. RIYA has 4 letters.
quiz.mistake: Finds the difference instead of the total

quiz.q: A class table says: 6 children have 4-letter names, 9 have 5-letter names and 4 have 6-letter names. Which name length is most common?
quiz.explain: 9 is the biggest count, so 5-letter names are the most common.
steps: Look at the counts: 4 letters → 6, 5 letters → 9, 6 letters → 4.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest name length (6) instead of the biggest count

quiz.q: Using the same table (6, 9 and 4 children), how many children are in the class?
quiz.explain: Add all the counts: 6 + 9 + 4 = 19 children.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the three groups

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know which friend has the longest name. How can he find out?
teach.praise: Yay! I counted all the letters and found the longest name!
teach.nudge: How do I know which name is the longest? What should I compare?

revise.summary: We count the letters in a name one by one. A table and tally marks help us see how many children have names of each length.
focus: Point and count every letter of a name.
Compare names to find the one with the most letters.
Read a table to find the most common name length.
remember: JOSEPH: J-1, O-2, S-3, E-4, P-5, H-6 = 6 letters.
Count a repeated letter every time: HARPREET has 8 letters.
traps: Don't count a repeated letter only once.
Don't skip or count a letter twice.
The most common length has the biggest count, not the biggest length.

learn.hook: Who is the captain? The animal with the longest name! Let us count letters.
points: Count the letters to see which name is longer or shorter.
Two different names can have the same number of letters: RAVI and NEHA both have 4.
To find the longest name in a class, count each name and pick the biggest count.
The shortest name has the smallest count. There may be a tie!
Fun fact: Venkatanarasimharajuvaripeta in Andhra Pradesh is one of India's longest railway station names. Ib in Odisha is one of the shortest.

example.q: Team captains must have the longest and the shortest names: CAT, ELEPHANT, PARROT, OWL. Who are they?
steps: Longest: ELEPHANT. Shortest: CAT and OWL tie at 3.
example.answer: ELEPHANT is longest; CAT and OWL tie for shortest

learn.reallife: When you fill a form with boxes for each letter, you need to know how many letters your name has!

quiz.q: Which animal has the LONGEST name?
quiz.explain: CROCODILE has 9 letters. LION 4, TIGER 5, ZEBRA 5.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest animal, not the longest name

quiz.q: Which bird has the SHORTEST name?
quiz.explain: EMU has 3 letters. CROW 4, SPARROW 7, PEACOCK 7.
quiz.mistake: Picks the smallest bird, not the shortest name

quiz.q: Which two names have the SAME number of letters?
quiz.explain: MEERA has 5 letters and KAVYA has 5 letters.
quiz.mistake: Thinks names must look alike to have the same length

quiz.q: How many more letters does ELEPHANT have than ANT?
quiz.explain: ELEPHANT has 8 letters and ANT has 3. 8 − 3 = 5.
steps: ELEPHANT has 8 letters. ANT has 3 letters.
How many more means take away the smaller from the bigger.
quiz.mistake: Gives the length of one name

quiz.q: Boys: AMAN, SIDDHARTH, VIR. Girls: PRIYA, LAKSHMI, ANU. Who has the longest name in the whole class?
quiz.explain: SIDDHARTH has 9 letters. LAKSHMI has only 7.
quiz.mistake: Only checks the girls' list

quiz.q: In the same class (AMAN, SIDDHARTH, VIR, PRIYA, LAKSHMI, ANU), which names are the shortest?
quiz.explain: VIR and ANU both have 3 letters. That is the least, so they tie.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that two names can tie

quiz.q: Fun fact: the station name VENKATANARASIMHARAJUVARIPETA (Andhra Pradesh) has 28 letters. IB (Odisha) has 2 letters. How many more letters does the long name have?
quiz.explain: 28 − 2 = 26 more letters.
steps: How many more means take away.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away

quiz.q: Reena says: 'Two different names can never have the same number of letters.' Is she right?
options: No, RAMU and GITA both have 4
Only if they start with the same letter
quiz.explain: Different names can have equal length. RAMU and GITA both have 4 letters.
steps: Answer: No, RAMU and GITA both have 4
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal length means the same name

teach.ask: Gappu wants to pick the bird with the longest name as captain. How does he find it?
teach.praise: Yay! Count letters, the most is longest and the fewest is shortest! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How do I know which name is the shortest?

revise.summary: Count the letters to find which name is longest or shortest. Two different names can have the same number of letters, so there may be a tie.
focus: Count each name and pick the biggest count for the longest.
Pick the smallest count for the shortest. Look for ties.
Find how many more letters by taking away.
remember: RAVI and NEHA both have 4 letters.
Longest = biggest count. Shortest = smallest count.
ELEPHANT 8 − ANT 3 = 5 more letters.
traps: Don't pick the biggest animal. Pick the longest name.
Don't forget that two names can tie.
Same length does not mean the same name.

learn.hook: How many friends share your first letter? Let us become letter detectives!
points: Write your friends' names in a list and look at the first letter of each.
Count names that start with the same letter as yours.
Find the starting letter that comes most often, and how many names begin with it.
We can also look at the last letter: RIYA, NEHA and ISHA all end with A.
Some letters, like Q, X or Z, may not start any name in the class.

example.q: Names: ARJUN, ANIL, BALA, ASHA, BHAVNA, CHETAN. Which starting letter is used most, and how many times?
steps: First letters: A, A, B, A, B, C.
A comes 3 times, B 2 times, C once.

learn.reallife: In the class register, names are written in ABC order using the first letter.

games.title: Start with A or end with A?

items.q: Names starting with S: SONU, SAM, RAJ
Names ending with I: RAVI, LILI, OM
Names starting with M: MINU, MOHAN, MANI
Names ending with N: ARJUN, KIRAN, ROHAN, ASHA
Names starting with K: KAVYA, DEV

quiz.q: Names: PRIYA, PAVAN, RAJ, POOJA. How many start with P?
quiz.explain: PRIYA, PAVAN and POOJA start with P. That is 3.
steps: Look at first letters: P, P, R, P
quiz.mistake: Counts all the names

quiz.q: Your name is MOHIT. Classmates: MEENA, SAHIL, MANOJ, KIRAN. How many classmates start with the same letter as you?
quiz.explain: MEENA and MANOJ start with M, like MOHIT.
steps: First letters: M, S, M, K
quiz.mistake: Counts own name too

quiz.q: Names: DIVYA, DEV, ANITA, DHRUV, AMAN. Which starting letter is used most often?
quiz.explain: D starts 3 names (DIVYA, DEV, DHRUV). A starts only 2.
quiz.mistake: Looks at last letters instead of first

quiz.q: In the same list (DIVYA, DEV, ANITA, DHRUV, AMAN), how many names start with the most-used letter?
quiz.explain: D is used most, and it starts 3 names.
quiz.mistake: Gives the count for A instead

quiz.q: Which name ENDS with the same letter as RIYA?
quiz.explain: RIYA ends with A. SHREYA also ends with A.
quiz.mistake: Matches the first letter instead of the last

quiz.q: Names: KABIR, SAMIR, ZAHIR, AMIT. How many end with R?
quiz.explain: KABIR, SAMIR and ZAHIR end with R. AMIT ends with T.
steps: Last letters: R, R, R, T
quiz.mistake: Counts names that have R anywhere

quiz.q: Names in a group: ANU, BINA, CHAND, DEEPA. Which letter from A to E begins NO name?
quiz.explain: A, B, C and D all start a name. No name starts with E.
steps: Starting letters: A, B, C, D
quiz.mistake: Checks last letters instead of first

quiz.q: Rohan's class list has 20 names. 4 start with S, 3 with A and 2 with R. Which letter starts the most names in this list?
quiz.explain: 4 is more than 3 and 2, so S starts the most names here.
quiz.mistake: Picks the first letter of the alphabet

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know which first letter is most popular among his bird friends. How should he find out?
teach.praise: Super! List names, look at the first letters, count, pick the most. Chirp!
teach.nudge: After I list the first letters, what do I do with them?

revise.summary: Look at the first letter of each name and count how many names start with the same letter. We can also look at the last letter.
focus: List the first letters and count each one.
Find the starting letter used most and how many times.
Check last letters too, like RIYA, NEHA and ISHA end with A.
remember: ARJUN, ANIL, BALA, ASHA, BHAVNA, CHETAN: A comes 3 times.
Some letters, like Q, X or Z, may not start any name.
traps: Don't mix up first letters with last letters.
Don't count names that only have the letter somewhere inside.

learn.hook: Teji and Jojo have number cards 4 and 7. They can make 47 or 74. Can you say both names?
points: Two number cards side by side make a 2-digit number. 4 and 7 make 47 or 74.
We write 47 as forty-seven. The tens word comes first, then the ones word.
Tens words: ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety.
Numbers 11 to 19 have special names: eleven, twelve, thirteen ... nineteen.
We can count the letters in a number name. Do not count the dash: forty-seven has 11 letters.

example.q: Your roll number is 23. How many letters are in its name?

learn.reallife: On a cheque or a money order, amounts are written in words so nobody can change them.

quiz.q: Teji has cards 3 and 8. Which two numbers can she make?
quiz.explain: Put 3 first to get 38, or 8 first to get 83.
quiz.mistake: Adds or multiplies the cards instead of placing them side by side

quiz.q: What is the number name of 56?
quiz.explain: 56 has 5 tens and 6 ones: fifty-six.
quiz.mistake: Reads the digits in the wrong order

quiz.q: Which number is 'ninety-one'?
quiz.explain: Ninety means 9 tens, and one means 1 one. That is 91.
quiz.mistake: Confuses ninety with nineteen

quiz.q: Which spelling is correct for 40?
quiz.explain: 40 is spelled F-O-R-T-Y, without a U.
quiz.mistake: Adds the U from 'four'

quiz.q: How many letters are in the name of 6?
quiz.explain: 6 is SIX: S, I, X. That is 3 letters.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number itself instead of the letter count

quiz.q: How many letters are in 'eighty-two' (do not count the dash)?
quiz.explain: EIGHTY has 6 letters and TWO has 3. 6 + 3 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Counts the dash as a letter

quiz.q: Jojo has cards 1 and 5. He makes the BIGGER number. What is its name?
quiz.explain: The bigger number is 51, fifty-one.
quiz.mistake: Puts the smaller digit in the tens place

quiz.q: Ananya's roll number is 17. How many letters are in its name?
quiz.explain: 17 is SEVENTEEN: S-E-V-E-N-T-E-E-N. That is 9 letters.
quiz.mistake: Counts only 'seven'

teach.ask: Gappu has cards 6 and 2. What numbers can he make and how does he say them?
teach.praise: Sixty-two and twenty-six! Same cards, two names! Chirp!
teach.nudge: Which card should go first to make the bigger number?

revise.summary: Two digit cards side by side make a 2-digit number, like 47. We write it as forty-seven: tens word first, then ones word.
focus: Make 2-digit numbers from two cards.
Write number names up to 99.
Count the letters in a number name, without the dash.
remember: Tens words: ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety.
11 to 19: eleven, twelve, thirteen ... nineteen.
forty-seven has 11 letters. twenty-three has 6 + 5 = 11 letters.
traps: Don't count the dash as a letter.
Forty has no U, even though four does.
Ninety (90) is not nineteen (19).

learn.hook: Which number between 1 and 99 has the longest name? Let us hunt!
points: Some number names have exactly 8 letters, like THIRTEEN (13) and FORTYONE (41).
Numbers 41, 42 and 46 all have 8-letter names. So do 51, 52, 56 and 61, 62, 66. Each is forty, fifty or sixty with one, two or six.
The longest names from 1 to 99 have 12 letters: seventy-three, seventy-seven and seventy-eight.
Riddles use clues about the number of letters and where the number lies.
Make your own puzzle: pick a number, count its letters and give clues.

example.q: I am between 10 and 20. My name has 7 letters. Who am I?
steps: Both fit, so a riddle needs one more clue, like 'I am odd': 15.

learn.reallife: Word games on number names are a fun way to practise spelling before a dictation test.

games.title: Name facts
items: THREE and SEVEN have the same number of letters.
The bigger the number, the longer its name.
70 (seventy, 7 letters) is bigger than 23 (twenty-three, 11 letters) but has a shorter name.
TEN and ONE have the same number of letters.

quiz.q: How many letters are in FOURTEEN?
quiz.explain: F-O-U-R-T-E-E-N has 8 letters.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number instead of the letter count

quiz.q: Which number has an 8-letter name?
quiz.explain: Forty-two: FORTY 5 + TWO 3 = 8 letters.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger number always has a longer name

quiz.q: Which of these does NOT have an 8-letter name?
quiz.explain: Thirty-five has THIRTY 6 + FIVE 4 = 10 letters. The others have 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the tens word

quiz.q: 41, 42, 46 have 8-letter names. 51, 52, 56 do too. What do these numbers share?
quiz.explain: Forty and fifty both have 5 letters, and one, two and six all have 3. So 5 + 3 = 8 each time.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at whether the number is odd or even

quiz.q: How many letters are in 'seventy-eight'?
quiz.explain: SEVENTY 7 + EIGHT 5 = 12. It is one of the longest names from 1 to 99.
quiz.mistake: Counts the dash

quiz.q: Which number from 1 to 99 has one of the LONGEST names?
quiz.explain: Seventy-seven has 12 letters. Ninety-nine has 10, eighty-eight 11.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the biggest number has the longest name

quiz.q: Riddle: I am between 1 and 10. My name has 4 letters. I am even. Who am I?
quiz.explain: 4-letter names under 10 are four, five and nine. Only 4 is even.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 'even' clue

quiz.q: Meera makes a puzzle: 'I am a tens number from 10 to 90 and my name has 7 letters.' What is the answer?
quiz.explain: SEVENTY has 7 letters. Sixty 5, forty 5, ninety 6.
quiz.mistake: Counts letters in the digit name only

teach.ask: Gappu asks: how can I find a number whose name has exactly 8 letters?
teach.praise: Forty-one, sixty-six, thirteen... I can find them all now! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How do I count the letters of a 2-digit name like forty-one?

revise.summary: Number-name puzzles use clues about how many letters a number name has and where the number lies. Count the letters to solve them.
focus: Count the letters in number names to solve riddles.
Use every clue, like between 10 and 20, odd or even.
Make your own puzzle with letter clues.
remember: THIRTEEN (13) and FORTYONE (41) have 8 letters.
Longest names from 1 to 99 have 12 letters: seventy-three, seventy-seven, seventy-eight.
traps: A bigger number does not always have a longer name.
Don't count the dash.
Don't forget a clue like 'I am even'.

learn.hook: A fan, a spoon and a TV walk into a room. Which ones need a plug?
points: We can sort things into two groups using a rule, like 'eats food' and 'does not eat food'.
Look at someone else's groups and find what is common in each group. That is their rule.
Things at home can be sorted as 'needs electricity' and 'does not need electricity'.
The same things can be regrouped with a new rule, like 'made of wood' or 'not made of wood'.
A good rule puts every object in exactly one group, with no object left out.

example.q: Sort: cow, chair, parrot, ball, fish. Rule: eats food / does not eat food.
steps: Cow, parrot and fish are living and eat food.
Chair and ball do not eat.
example.answer: Eats food: cow, parrot, fish. Does not: chair, ball

learn.reallife: At home we sort clothes into 'to wash' and 'clean', and shopkeepers sort fruits and vegetables.

games.title: Is the rule good?
items: 'Eats food / does not eat food' puts a goat and a stone in different groups.
A goat eats; a stone does not.
A good rule can leave some objects without a group.
Every object must fit in exactly one group.
The same things can be sorted again with a new rule.
For example by colour, then by size.
A ball can be in both 'round' and 'not round'.

quiz.q: Which of these needs electricity to work?
quiz.explain: A ceiling fan runs on electricity. The others do not.
steps: Check each thing: does it need electricity to work?
Broom, bucket and comb work by hand.
A ceiling fan has a switch and runs on electricity.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything at home needs electricity

quiz.q: Group 1: dog, hen, fish. Group 2: table, cup, shoe. What is the rule?
options: Eats food and does not eat food
quiz.explain: Dog, hen and fish are animals that eat food. Table, cup and shoe do not.
steps: Group 2: all things that do not
Answer: Eats food and does not eat food
quiz.mistake: Looks at size instead of what is common

quiz.q: Which object belongs in the 'does not eat food' group?
quiz.explain: A kite is a thing, not a living being. It does not eat.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the bird kite with the paper kite

quiz.q: Group A: fridge, TV, mixer. Group B: broom, chair, plate. What is common in Group A?
options: They are all made of wood
They are all in the kitchen
quiz.explain: A fridge, a TV and a mixer all run on electricity.
steps: Look at Group A: fridge, TV, mixer.
They are not made of wood and are not all in the kitchen (TV is not).
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the room they are kept in

quiz.q: Ravi sorts: spoon, plate, glass, chair. He uses a NEW rule: 'made of steel' / 'not made of steel'. Where does the wooden chair go?
quiz.explain: The wooden chair is not steel, so it goes in 'not made of steel'.
quiz.mistake: Puts an object in both groups

quiz.q: Why is 'big things / red things' a poor rule for sorting?
options: A big red bus fits both groups
quiz.explain: A good rule puts each object in exactly one group. A big red bus fits both, so the rule is confusing.
steps: Big red bus: big? yes. Red? yes.
Answer: A big red bus fits both groups
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two labels make a good rule

quiz.q: Sort 6 things: fan, lamp, TV, bat, ball, cap by 'needs electricity'. How many go in the 'needs electricity' group?
quiz.explain: Fan, lamp and TV need electricity. That is 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts all the things

quiz.q: Leela sorted toys first by colour. Now she sorts them by 'has wheels / no wheels'. What is true?
options: The same toys can be sorted in a new way
quiz.explain: The same objects can be regrouped with a different rule.
steps: Answer: The same toys can be sorted in a new way
quiz.mistake: Thinks objects belong to one group forever

teach.ask: Gappu has a pile of things: a fan, a feather, a TV and a nest. How can he sort them into two groups?
teach.praise: I made a rule: needs electricity or not! Every thing has one group. Chirp!
teach.nudge: What rule did you use to decide which group each thing goes in?

revise.summary: We sort things into two groups using a rule, like 'needs electricity' or 'does not need electricity'. We can find someone's rule by seeing what is common in each group.
focus: Sort things into two groups by a rule.
Find the rule by looking at what is common.
Regroup the same things with a new rule.
remember: Eats food: cow, parrot, fish. Does not: chair, ball.
A good rule puts every object in exactly one group, with none left out.
traps: Don't put one object in both groups.
Not everything at home needs electricity.
Objects do not stay in one group forever. A new rule makes new groups.

learn.hook: Plaits, ponytails, short hair, buns... which style is the class favourite?
points: A survey means looking at or asking every child about one thing, like their hairstyle.
Record each child's style with a tally mark next to the style name.
Then write the totals in a simple table.
The style with the biggest number is the most common. The smallest number is the least common.
Add all the numbers to check that every child was counted once.

example.q: Table: Plait 8, Ponytail 5, Short hair 12, Bun 3. Which style is most common and which is least?

learn.reallife: Schools do surveys to find out how children come to school, like by bus, cycle or walking.

games.title: Read the table: Plait 7, Ponytail 4, Short 10, Bun 2

items.q: How many more short than plait?

quiz.q: Survey: Plait 6, Ponytail 9, Short hair 11, Bun 2. Which style is most common?
quiz.explain: 11 is the biggest number, so short hair is most common.
quiz.mistake: Picks the first row

quiz.q: Same survey (6, 9, 11, 2). Which style is least common?
quiz.explain: 2 is the smallest number, so bun is least common.
steps: The least common style has the smallest number.
The smallest number is 2, for bun.
quiz.mistake: Picks the most common by mistake

quiz.q: Same survey (6, 9, 11, 2). How many children are in the class?
quiz.explain: 6 + 9 + 11 + 2 = 28 children.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out one row

quiz.q: Tally for ponytails shows 1 bundle of five and 3 lines. How many children have ponytails?
quiz.explain: A bundle is 5. 5 + 3 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Counts the bundle as 1

quiz.q: In a survey, why must we look at EVERY child in the class?
options: So that the counts are true for the whole class
So that the table is long
quiz.explain: If some children are missed, the totals will be wrong.
steps: A survey must count each child once.
If some children are missed, the totals will be wrong.
Counting every child makes the counts true for the whole class.
Answer: So that the counts are true for the whole class
quiz.mistake: Thinks a few children are enough

quiz.q: Survey: Plait 9, Short 9, Bun 4. Which is true?
options: Plait and short are equally common
quiz.explain: Plait and short both have 9. They are tied as most common.
steps: Answer: Plait and short are equally common
quiz.mistake: Picks one of the tied rows

quiz.q: Plait 10, Ponytail 6. How many more children have plaits than ponytails?
quiz.explain: 10 − 6 = 4 more children have plaits.
steps: How many more means take away.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: A class has 30 children. The table shows Plait 12, Short 10, Ponytail 5. How many children are NOT in these three rows?
quiz.explain: 12 + 10 + 5 = 27. 30 − 27 = 3 children have some other style.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to take away from the class total

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know which feather colour is most common in his flock. How should he do a survey?
teach.praise: Look at every bird, tally, make a table, then read the biggest number! Chirp!
teach.nudge: How will I write the counts neatly so I can read them later?

revise.summary: A survey asks every child about one thing, like their hairstyle. We record it with tally marks, make a table and find the most and least common.
focus: Record survey answers with tally marks.
Find the most common (biggest number) and least common (smallest number).
Find how many more by taking away.
remember: Most common = biggest number. Least common = smallest number.
Add all the numbers to check every child was counted once.
traps: Don't count a tally bundle as 1. It is 5.
Don't leave out a row when adding.
Don't add when the question asks how many more.

learn.hook: Who has more laddoos, you or your cousin? Maths can settle it fairly!
points: To compare, we find out which group is more, which is fewer, or if they are the same.
Line up two groups one-to-one. Things left over show which group has more.
To find HOW MANY more, take the smaller number away from the bigger one.
We can also count on from the smaller number to the bigger number.

example.q: Kabir has 12 marbles. Meena has 8 marbles. How many more marbles does Kabir have?
steps: The bigger number is 12, the smaller is 8.
Count on from 8 to 12: 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 4 steps.

learn.reallife: At a market, you compare prices to see which shop is cheaper, and in cricket you compare scores to see who won.

games.title: Line up the scores
games.prompt: Arrange the runs from fewest to most

quiz.q: Riya has 14 bangles. Aisha has 9 bangles. How many more bangles does Riya have?
quiz.explain: Take the smaller number from the bigger one: 14 − 9 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Which box has the FEWEST crayons?
quiz.explain: 18 is the smallest of 18, 24, 31 and 20, so that box has the fewest crayons.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up fewer with more

quiz.q: Arjun scored 25 runs and Kabir scored 32 runs. How many more runs did Kabir score?
quiz.explain: 32 − 25 = 7. Count on from 25: 26 ... 30 is 5, then 31, 32 is 2 more. 5 + 2 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Counts one step too many when counting on

quiz.q: Meena has 16 stickers. Joseph has 16 stickers too. What is true?
quiz.explain: Both have 16, so neither has more. They have the same number.
steps: Answer: They have the same number
quiz.mistake: Thinks one person must always have more

quiz.q: Harpreet has 10 diyas. She needs 18 diyas for Diwali. How many more diyas does she need?
quiz.explain: From 10 to 18 is 8 more. So 18 − 10 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 and 18 instead of finding what is missing

quiz.q: A basket has 21 bananas and another has 12 bananas. Which is correct?
quiz.explain: 21 has 2 tens and 12 has only 1 ten, so 21 is more.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit (1 and 2) instead of the tens

quiz.q: Aisha has 6 fewer pencils than Riya. Riya has 15 pencils. How many does Aisha have?
quiz.explain: Fewer means take away: 15 − 6 = 9 pencils.
quiz.mistake: Adds when the word 'fewer' means take away

quiz.q: Kabir has 4 more toy cars than Arjun. Arjun has 11. How many toy cars does Kabir have?
quiz.explain: 4 more than 11 is 11 + 4 = 15.
steps: Kabir has 4 more than Arjun, so add.
quiz.mistake: Takes away when the question says 'more'

teach.ask: Gappu has 7 worms and his sister has 10. He wants to know how many more she has. Can you help?
teach.praise: Now I know she has 3 more worms. I will ask her to share!
teach.nudge: I know she has more. But how do I find HOW MANY more?

revise.summary: To compare, find which group is more, fewer or the same. To find how many more, take the smaller number from the bigger one or count on.
focus: Say which number is more or fewer.
Find how many more by taking away or counting on.
Find a total when someone has 'more than' another.
remember: How many more = bigger − smaller.
Compare tens first: 21 has 2 tens, 12 has 1 ten.
traps: Don't add the two numbers to find the difference.
Don't mix up fewer and more.
If the question says '4 more than 11', add: 11 + 4.
